scope.evidence_basis: Only the snippets provided in the request. No repository inspection, no tools, no code execution, no test runs, no device interaction.
scope.authorization_status: Design only. No native permissions were requested or granted, no camera capture or file write was performed, and no remote command was authorized or executed.
constraints: Do not claim headless capture works.
Do not remove or degrade the existing CameraScreen camera feature.
Do not introduce a new permission engine, command engine, handler registry, or operation engine.
Remote commands must stay inside the existing authorization/dispatch path.
No actual device or native permission action is authorized by this proposal.

findings.issue: Calls the nonexistent top-level API `Camera.takePictureAsync(...)`. In the CameraView-generation expo-camera API, `takePictureAsync` is an instance method of a mounted `CameraView`; the top-level `Camera` object does not expose it.
findings.consequence: Every remote `camera_snap` fails at runtime with a TypeError and is reported as a generic capture failure. No photo is produced. This path must not be described as working or simulated with a fake result.

findings.issue: The service requires the caller to pass `React.RefObject<CameraView>` but stores no reference to the currently mounted camera. The only valid capture surface is the local `cameraRef` inside `CameraScreen.tsx`, which is never shared. There is no registration API.
findings.consequence: `deviceSocket` has no legitimate way to obtain the mounted view. Any implementation that invents a global ref or calls a top-level capture API is either broken or a hidden headless-capture claim.

findings.issue: `quality: command.params.quality || 0.8` coerces a valid `quality` value of `0` to `0.8`. Zero is a real, useful setting meaning maximum compression.
findings.consequence: The remote command cannot request quality 0. The intended request is silently altered. Use nullish/default semantics only for `undefined` or `null`.

findings.issue: A default `savePath` under `FileSystem.cacheDirectory` is constructed unconditionally, but `FileSystem.copyAsync` runs only when `command.params.save_path` is supplied. The result then reports `file_path: savePath` even though that file was never created.
findings.consequence: Consumers receive a fabricated path and may fail to read it or mistake it for a captured artifact. The actual file is `result.uri`, and after `CameraService` post-processing it may be a different URI again.

findings.issue: The socket handler calls `Camera.requestCameraPermissionsAsync()` directly. This duplicates the service's permission authority and can raise an OS permission prompt in response to a remote command, without a foreground user gesture.
findings.consequence: A remote command can trigger permission UI and bypasses the intended screen/service permission flow. It is also not a substitute for capture-time revalidation.

findings.issue: `permissionStatus` is cached from `initialize`, `requestPermissions`, or `getPermissionStatus`, but `takePicture` checks only the cached value. It is not refreshed at capture time.
findings.consequence: If the user revokes camera permission in OS settings while the screen is mounted, the cached value can remain `granted`. The command may attempt capture under a stale authorization assumption instead of failing closed.

findings.issue: There is no mount, readiness, or unmount lifecycle exposed to the service. `CameraView` may be mounted but not ready, and an unmount leaves no shared state that a command can consult.
findings.consequence: Capture can be attempted against a view that is not ready or no longer mounted. Failures are nondeterministic. The correct behavior is explicit `not_mounted` or `not_ready` failure, never queuing, retrying, or pretending success.

findings.issue: `takePicture` catches every error and returns `null`. The caller cannot distinguish missing ref, permission denial, readiness failure, or native capture failure.
findings.consequence: `deviceSocket` can only emit a generic error. The mounted-view entry point needs a small typed error taxonomy; the existing `takePicture` null contract can remain for `CameraScreen` compatibility.

findings.issue: The socket result expects `base64_data`, but `PhotoOptions` does not include `base64`. If base64 is requested from the native call while the service also resizes or compresses the image, the base64 may describe a different image than the returned file URI.
findings.consequence: The wire payload and the stored file can disagree. Either derive base64 from the final returned URI, or explicitly change the contract and coordinate with consumers.

findings.issue: When the image exceeds `MAX_IMAGE_DIMENSION`, `ImageManipulator.manipulateAsync` re-encodes with fixed `COMPRESSION_QUALITY`, not the caller-supplied quality.
findings.consequence: A capture requested with `quality: 0` can be partially undone by post-processing. The exact constant values are not visible in the snippet, but the control flow is clear. This matters specifically for honoring quality 0 end-to-end.

findings.issue: `fileInfo.size` is read from the native photo before compression. If `finalUri` is the compressed file, `media.size` can describe the pre-compression file.
findings.consequence: Reported metadata can be inconsistent with the URI the consumer receives. Re-stat `finalUri` after post-processing.

findings.issue: An unused map exists, but there is no registration API and no population path. It is not an extension point that can be switched on.
findings.consequence: Turning it into a general handler registry would add a second dispatch mechanism and still would not solve camera-view ownership. Do not implement or advertise it as part of this change.

findings.issue: `command.params.quality` is dereferenced without optional chaining, and the value is not validated as a number in the 0..1 range.
findings.consequence: Malformed or absent params produce avoidable errors or are forwarded without validation. Use `command.params?.` and validate before forwarding.

findings.issue: `Camera.requestCameraPermissionsAsync` still exists even though `Camera.takePictureAsync` does not. Removing the whole camera import may be wrong if other command paths legitimately use permission APIs.
findings.consequence: Remove only the capture call and the socket-level permission request. Verify remaining references before pruning imports.

existing_mechanism_to_reuse.reuse: Make the existing service the single owner of the mounted view and the single capture entry point. Do not create a parallel camera manager.
Extract the existing capture/file-info/compression/media assembly into one private core used by both the current ref-based API and the new mounted-view API. This preserves `CameraScreen` behavior.
The actual `CameraView` instance is the only valid capture handle. Reuse `onCameraReady` for readiness and the existing `useRef` as the registered instance.
Extend additively with optional `base64` fields rather than inventing new media or result models. Existing `CameraScreen` callers remain valid.
Reuse `Camera.getCameraPermissionsAsync()` and the existing mapping for capture-time revalidation. Do not add a new permission model.
Keep the existing command switch and result shape. Replace only the broken capture body. The camera handler remains under the same dispatch and authorization path.
Use the same APIs for explicit saves, post-processing metadata, and optional base64 derivation. Do not add a file-operation engine.
Use a per-registration opaque token and cleanup on unmount. This is the stale-unmount guard; no new lifecycle system is needed.

types.MountedCameraToken: Opaque per-registration identity token, for example a symbol. Not serializable, not a permission token, not an authorization credential.
types.CameraCaptureError: Local error type carrying one of the codes above. This is not a permission or command engine.

api.semantics: Stores the exact mounted view instance, creates a new token, resets readiness to false, and returns the token. Last registration wins. A previous token becomes stale.
Sets readiness only if the token is still current. A stale token is a no-op. Does not request permissions.
Clears the mounted view and readiness only if the token is still current. A stale unmount from an older registration cannot clear a newer view.

Requires a current mounted view, readiness true, and a fresh OS permission check of granted. Captures on the exact registered instance and returns the actual final URI. Throws CameraCaptureError with a specific code; never invents a URI.
Existing API preserved for CameraScreen. Internally uses the same capture core. Keeps the null-on-error behavior for compatibility.

capture_options.quality: Forwarded exactly. `0` must remain `0`. Default only when the value is undefined or null.
capture_options.base64: Optional additive flag. If true, derive base64 from the final returned URI so the payload matches the stored file.
capture_options.post_processing_quality: When resizing/compressing, use the caller-supplied quality when present, falling back to the existing COMPRESSION_QUALITY constant only when absent.

invariants: Only `CameraView.takePictureAsync` on the exact registered instance is used for capture.
A capture is possible only when a current token exists, readiness is true, and a fresh permission check returns granted.
A stale `markReady` or `unregister` call is a no-op and cannot affect a newer registration.
Readiness is not inferred from mount. It must be explicitly marked from `onCameraReady`.
Capture fails deterministically with `not_mounted` or `not_ready`; it does not queue, poll, retry, or fabricate a result.
The socket never calls `requestCameraPermissionsAsync` and never changes facing, flash, mode, or other camera configuration.
`file_path` is always a real artifact: the actual final capture URI, or an explicit save destination only after a successful copy.
No explicit save means no default copy and no fabricated cache path.
Base64, when present, is derived from the final file URI, not from an earlier unprocessed capture.

data.base64_data: optional string, present when a base64 capture was requested

success.file_path: actual final capture URI, or the explicit save_path only after copyAsync resolves

failure.error: specific, stable message derived from CameraCaptureError.code or the save failure

socket_result_contract.compatibility_note: The top-level result shape remains unchanged. The semantic change is that `file_path` is now truthful instead of always a guessed cache path. Backend consumers must not assume a cache-directory prefix.

implementation_plan.change: Add `MountedCameraToken`, `CameraCaptureErrorCode`, and `CameraCaptureError`. Add private fields for the current view, current token, and ready flag. Add `registerMountedView`, `markMountedViewReady`, and `unregisterMountedView` with strict token-identity checks.
implementation_plan.notes: Registration replaces any previous registration. Readiness starts false. Unregister only clears if the supplied token is current.

implementation_plan.change: Extract the existing capture body into a private `captureWithView(view, options)` that performs the native `takePictureAsync`, file info, optional compression, and media assembly. Add a separate `assertFreshPermission()` that calls `Camera.getCameraPermissionsAsync()`, updates `permissionStatus`, and throws `CameraCaptureError('permission_denied')` unless the fresh status is granted.
implementation_plan.notes: `assertFreshPermission` never prompts. It fails closed on API error. `takePicture` becomes a thin wrapper preserving ref validation, logging, and null-on-error behavior.

implementation_plan.change: Implement `captureFromMountedView(options)` with this order: snapshot view and token; fail `not_mounted` if absent; fail `not_ready` if readiness is false; await fresh permission; re-check token and view identity; call `captureWithView`; throw `capture_failed` if no media; return media.
implementation_plan.notes: The post-await identity re-check prevents an unmount during permission revalidation from silently targeting a replaced view. An in-flight native capture cannot be cancelled; do not add cancellation infrastructure.

implementation_plan.change: Honor caller quality in post-processing: use `options.quality ?? COMPRESSION_QUALITY` in the ImageManipulator compression step, and re-stat `finalUri` after compression so `media.size` matches the returned file. When `base64` is requested, read the final URI as base64.
implementation_plan.notes: This is a behavior change for callers that previously supplied a quality but were re-encoded at the fixed constant. Flag it in the commit message. It is required for quality 0 to survive end-to-end.

implementation_plan.change: Keep `cameraRef` and all existing UI/permission-flows intact. Add a mounted-token ref and a ready ref. In an effect keyed on `permission?.granted`, register `cameraRef.current`, store the token, apply an already-fired readiness signal, and return a cleanup that unregisters that exact token and clears local refs. Wire `onCameraReady` to set the ready ref and call `markMountedViewReady(token)` when a token exists.
implementation_plan.notes: Do not add focus-based gating, remote mode switching, or a second permission prompt. If `cameraRef.current` is not available in the effect, do not register; the readiness ref re-applies on the next successful registration. Reset the ready ref on cleanup.

implementation_plan.change: Rewrite `handleCameraSnap` to call `cameraService.captureFromMountedView`. Use `const params = command.params ?? {}`. Forward `params.quality` only when it is a number in 0..1, with a default of 0.8 only for undefined/null. Pass `exif: true` and the existing base64 requirement through the additive option. Remove the socket-level permission request and the top-level capture call.
implementation_plan.notes: Special-case quality 0 explicitly in tests. Do not call `Camera.requestCameraPermissionsAsync`. Preserve the existing result shape and timestamp format.

implementation_plan.change: Remove the unconditional default `save_path`. Set `filePath = media.uri`. If and only if a non-empty explicit `save_path` is supplied, await `FileSystem.copyAsync({ from: media.uri, to: params.save_path })` and then set `filePath = params.save_path`. On copy failure, return `success: false` and do not report a file path.
implementation_plan.notes: Copy failure is a command failure even though the native capture succeeded. Do not silently create parent directories unless that becomes an explicit, reviewed policy.

implementation_plan.change: Map `CameraCaptureError.code` to stable messages: `not_mounted` -> `Camera is not open on the device`; `not_ready` -> `Camera is not ready yet`; `permission_denied` -> `Camera permission not granted`; `capture_failed` -> the underlying capture message. Keep generic fallback handling for unexpected errors.
implementation_plan.notes: Do not expose a fake success or a guessed file path for any error case.

implementation_plan.change: Leave the unused handler map untouched. Do not add handler registration, a new dispatcher, or a new command path. Optionally remove the dead map in a separate cleanup after confirming no external references.
implementation_plan.notes: The mounted-view registration in CameraService is the chosen mechanism. The unused map is neither needed nor sufficient.

implementation_plan.change: Verify how the backend consumes `file_path` and `base64_data`. Confirm it does not assume `file_path` is always under the mobile cache directory and that it can handle the actual final URI. No backend code change is proposed here.
implementation_plan.notes: If the backend requires a stable cache path, that is a wire-contract decision to resolve explicitly rather than by lying in the result.

decisive_tests.name: No top-level capture API remains
decisive_tests.setup: Search mobile sources for `Camera.takePictureAsync` and for `requestCameraPermissionsAsync` in deviceSocket.
assertions: No `Camera.takePictureAsync` occurrence remains in the camera command path.
The only capture call is `takePictureAsync` on a mounted CameraView instance.
decisive_tests.why_decisive: Directly proves the broken API path is gone and the remote command cannot trigger a permission prompt.

decisive_tests.name: Mounted view is the exact registered instance
decisive_tests.setup: Create fake CameraView A and B with jest mock `takePictureAsync`. Register A, mark A ready, capture.
assertions: Returned media.uri equals A's resolved URI.
decisive_tests.why_decisive: Proves capture ownership is explicit and does not depend on a global ref or top-level API.

decisive_tests.name: Stale unmount cannot clear a newer view
decisive_tests.setup: Register A -> tokenA. Register B -> tokenB. Call unregister(tokenA). Mark tokenB ready. Capture.
decisive_tests.why_decisive: This is the stale-unmount requirement. A naive boolean or ref cleanup fails this test.

decisive_tests.name: Stale readiness is ignored
decisive_tests.setup: Register A -> tokenA. Register B -> tokenB. Call markMountedViewReady(tokenA). Capture without marking tokenB ready.
decisive_tests.why_decisive: Proves readiness is bound to the current registration, not to a global or stale callback.

decisive_tests.name: Capture before readiness fails closed
decisive_tests.setup: Register and do not call markReady. Attempt capture.
assertions: No fake media or path is returned.
decisive_tests.why_decisive: Prevents a mounted-but-not-ready view from producing a nondeterministic native failure or a simulated success.

decisive_tests.name: Capture after unmount fails closed
decisive_tests.setup: Register, mark ready, unregister with the current token. Attempt capture.
decisive_tests.why_decisive: Proves unmount gating and confirms no headless fallback exists.

decisive_tests.name: Permission is revalidated at capture time
decisive_tests.setup: Register and mark ready. Mock `Camera.getCameraPermissionsAsync` to return denied. Attempt capture.
decisive_tests.why_decisive: Covers OS revocation after screen mount and proves the command does not prompt or bypass authorization.

decisive_tests.name: Permission granted allows capture and updates cached state
decisive_tests.setup: Register and mark ready. Mock fresh permission as granted. Capture.
assertions: The service's cached permission status is `granted`.
decisive_tests.why_decisive: Verifies reauthorization is a fresh check, not a stale cached assumption, and that it does not introduce prompting.

decisive_tests.name: Quality 0 is preserved
decisive_tests.setup: Call the socket handler with `params.quality = 0`, or call the service capture path with `quality: 0`. Assert the native option.
assertions: If post-processing runs, the manipulator compression value is 0, not COMPRESSION_QUALITY.
decisive_tests.why_decisive: This is the explicit quality-0 requirement and catches both the truthiness bug and the later re-encode bug.

decisive_tests.name: Quality defaults only when absent
decisive_tests.setup: Call with quality undefined, then with quality 0.5.
assertions: Null is treated like undefined; 0 is never treated as absent.
decisive_tests.why_decisive: Verifies the fallback semantics are precise.

decisive_tests.name: No explicit save means no copy and a real URI
decisive_tests.setup: Capture with fake media URI `file:///cache/final.jpg` and no save_path.
assertions: `file_path` does not equal any invented `${cacheDirectory}camera_<id>.jpg` path.
decisive_tests.why_decisive: Catches the fabricated-path bug directly.

decisive_tests.name: Explicit save reports success only after copy resolves
decisive_tests.setup: Capture with media URI `file:///cache/final.jpg` and explicit save_path `file:///docs/snap.jpg`. Mock copyAsync resolve.
assertions: copyAsync is called with `{ from: media.uri, to: save_path }`.
The result is success only after the promise resolves.
decisive_tests.why_decisive: Proves explicit-save semantics and prevents optimistic success.

decisive_tests.name: Explicit save failure is a command failure
decisive_tests.setup: Mock copyAsync to reject.
assertions: The error indicates the save failure rather than a capture failure.
decisive_tests.why_decisive: Prevents reporting a path that was never written.

decisive_tests.name: Base64 matches the returned file
decisive_tests.setup: Mock post-processing to return a compressed URI; request base64. Make readAsStringAsync return known base64 for the final URI.
assertions: `base64_data` is derived from the final URI.
`base64_data` does not come from the pre-compression native image.
decisive_tests.why_decisive: Prevents the payload from describing a different image than `file_path`.

decisive_tests.name: Missing params are safe
decisive_tests.setup: Call `handleCameraSnap` with `params` undefined.
assertions: No TypeError is thrown for `params.quality` or `params.save_path`.
decisive_tests.why_decisive: Covers malformed remote commands without widening the command contract.

decisive_tests.name: Existing takePicture behavior is preserved
decisive_tests.setup: Call `cameraService.takePicture` with a ref containing a fake view, then with a null ref.
assertions: Valid ref returns CapturedMedia with the actual URI.
Permission denial returns null, preserving the existing local caller contract.
decisive_tests.why_decisive: Confirms the camera feature used by CameraScreen was not broken by the refactor.

decisive_tests.name: Foreground CameraScreen explicit save
decisive_tests.setup: Open CameraScreen, grant permission, let onCameraReady fire, send camera_snap with a save_path under an app-writable directory.
assertions: The returned file_path exists and is readable on the device.
Image dimensions match the returned width/height.
The camera preview is not removed or reconfigured.
decisive_tests.why_decisive: Verifies the actual native boundary and proves the result is not a fabricated cache path.

decisive_tests.name: No save_path returns a real temporary URI
decisive_tests.setup: Send camera_snap without save_path.
assertions: file_path is the actual captured file URI.
No copy operation is performed and no nonexistent path is returned.
decisive_tests.why_decisive: Verifies the corrected no-save contract end to end.

decisive_tests.name: Quality 0 is observably honored
decisive_tests.setup: Capture the same static scene twice through the command path: quality 0 and quality 0.8, with post-processing controlled.
assertions: The provided quality reaches the native capture and any post-processing step.
The quality-0 artifact is not silently normalized to 0.8.
decisive_tests.why_decisive: A unit mock can verify forwarding, but an on-device check catches platform normalization or post-processing overrides.

decisive_tests.name: No CameraScreen means explicit failure
decisive_tests.setup: Navigate away or unmount CameraScreen. Send camera_snap.
assertions: Result is `success: false` with a `not_mounted` style message.
No file is fabricated or reported.
decisive_tests.why_decisive: Directly enforces 'never pretend headless capture works'.

decisive_tests.name: OS permission revocation fails closed without prompting
decisive_tests.setup: Open CameraScreen, revoke camera permission in OS settings, return to the app without re-granting, send camera_snap.
assertions: Command fails with a permission message.
No OS permission prompt is raised by the remote command.
decisive_tests.why_decisive: Verifies capture-time reauthorization and proves the remote path cannot prompt or bypass permission.

decisive_tests.name: Unauthorized socket session cannot reach the camera handler
decisive_tests.setup: Use the existing socket authentication/authorization test harness to send a camera_snap without valid authorization.
assertions: The existing authorization layer rejects the command before handler execution.
No new authorization bypass is introduced.
decisive_tests.why_decisive: Ensures the change stays inside the existing authorization boundary. If the harness does not exist, this test is blocked and must be resolved as a governance issue before shipping.

decisive_tests.name: Unmount during permission revalidation does not target a replacement view
decisive_tests.setup: Begin capture, delay the permission promise, unregister and register a new view during the await, then resolve permission.
assertions: The old capture attempt does not call the new view's takePictureAsync.
The attempt fails with `not_mounted` or otherwise targets only the snapshot it started with.
decisive_tests.why_decisive: Covers the async race between permission revalidation and view replacement.

unresolved_authorization_governance.issue: The provided `deviceSocket` snippet does not show a per-command authorization check. It is unknown whether the socket handshake or pairing layer authorizes all commands, camera commands specifically, or neither.
unresolved_authorization_governance.decision_needed: Confirm which existing layer authorizes remote commands and whether camera capture requires a distinct scope or explicit user consent. Do not invent a new authority inside CameraService.
unresolved_authorization_governance.default_in_this_proposal: Keep `handleCameraSnap` inside the existing `handleCommand` dispatch and add no new authorization logic. If command-level authorization does not exist, treat this as a blocker for shipping, not as a camera-service problem.

unresolved_authorization_governance.issue: A mounted CameraScreen is only a weak signal of user presence or consent. The screen may remain open while the user is elsewhere, and registration is based on mount, not focus or recent interaction.
unresolved_authorization_governance.decision_needed: Decide whether capture requires a focused screen, recent user interaction, a visible indicator, or a time-bound consent window. Focus gating or timeouts are policy changes, not implementation details.
unresolved_authorization_governance.default_in_this_proposal: Register on mount and unregister on unmount only. Do not add focus or interaction gating silently.

unresolved_authorization_governance.issue: `save_path` is remote-caller-controlled. A successful copy can write to any path the app can access, which is a write and potential exfiltration primitive.
unresolved_authorization_governance.decision_needed: Decide whether to restrict saves to app-owned directories, normalize paths, or use an allowlist. This is a security contract change and can break existing integrations.
unresolved_authorization_governance.default_in_this_proposal: Preserve existing save semantics, perform the copy only when explicitly requested, and surface failures. Do not silently add a path policy as part of the camera fix.

unresolved_authorization_governance.issue: Base64 image data and EXIF are transmitted over the socket. EXIF may include location and device metadata. Retention and logging are unspecified.
unresolved_authorization_governance.decision_needed: Decide whether EXIF should be stripped, whether base64 is required at all, and what retention/audit rules apply.
unresolved_authorization_governance.default_in_this_proposal: Preserve the existing `exif: true` and base64 result shape for compatibility. Do not add a new telemetry or audit subsystem.

unresolved_authorization_governance.issue: Headless capture is not possible with this architecture. Without a mounted foreground CameraView, there is no valid native capture session.
unresolved_authorization_governance.decision_needed: Product must accept 'camera screen open' as a hard requirement, or separately design a foreground/native capability with its own authorization, platform constraints, and store-review implications.
unresolved_authorization_governance.default_in_this_proposal: Return an explicit not-mounted failure. Do not attempt background capture or simulate it.

unresolved_authorization_governance.issue: If permission is missing, the proposal fails the command rather than prompting. A remote command must not raise an OS permission dialog without a user gesture.
unresolved_authorization_governance.decision_needed: If the product requires automatic recovery, decide how a foreground user gesture is obtained. That is a UX and consent decision, not something the camera service should do on behalf of a remote command.
unresolved_authorization_governance.default_in_this_proposal: Revalidate only; never call `requestCameraPermissionsAsync` from the socket. Existing CameraScreen permission flow remains the acquisition path.

unresolved_authorization_governance.issue: If multiple CameraViews can be mounted at once, last-registration-wins means the older screen loses capture and the remote command may target the most recently mounted instance.
unresolved_authorization_governance.decision_needed: Confirm whether multiple camera screens can coexist. If they can, define the ownership policy explicitly; do not build an arbitration engine implicitly.

unresolved_authorization_governance.issue: Changing `file_path` from a guessed cache path to the actual final URI, and deriving base64 from the final file, is a wire-contract semantic change.
unresolved_authorization_governance.decision_needed: Confirm backend compatibility and versioning. If consumers require a cache path, define a real normalization step rather than returning a path that was never written.
unresolved_authorization_governance.default_in_this_proposal: Return truthful paths and align base64 with the returned file. No backend code change is part of this proposal.

explicit_non_goals: No new command dispatcher, operation engine, or permission engine.
No headless capture, background capture, or fallback that fakes a camera result.
No remote changes to camera facing, flash, or mode.
No removal of CameraScreen or its local capture feature.
No new native dependency or native module.
No backend changes in this proposal.
No claim that any test, build, or device flow has been run.
